summary: Retest of Stack.jsx desktop-drag double-fire fix (useRef didDragRef guard set in onDragStart, checked in onTap, cleared in onDragEnd via 50ms setTimeout). ALL requested test cases PASS: (1) Desktop 3-drag round-trip on 3-image stack — each drag shifts by exactly 1, round-trip restores initial image. (2) Isolated tap cycles by exactly 1. (3) Mixed sequence (drag→tap→drag→tap) — each of 4 actions shifts by exactly 1. (4) Mobile viewport (390x844) single drag shifts by 1. (5) Grep verification of Stack.jsx: useRef, didDragRef, onDragStart, and didDragRef.current guard in onTap ALL present. Iteration_4's HIGH bug is FIXED.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal and correct: useRef flag set in onDragStart, checked-and-bailed in onTap, cleared in a 50ms setTimeout after onDragEnd — matches the exact recommendation from iteration_4. No unintended side-effects observed.

The 50ms clearing window is long enough for framer-motion's late onTap after mouse drag but short enough that subsequent legit taps register (validated in mixed sequence test — tap immediately after a drag still fires exactly once).

Optional (LOW, unchanged from iteration_4): Rotation is deterministic and visible (~4-5 degrees per screenshot) but resting computed transform reads ~0.3 degrees due to framer spring interpolation sampling; purely cosmetic, not a functional issue.
